ordered_diagnoses: Squamous cell carcinoma of the anus

s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic perianal disease with recent worsening of symptoms and development of mucinous discharge, pain, and perianal induration
salient_findings: Internal fistula opening at the dentate line
key_facts: History of incision and drainage of a recurrent perianal abscess
Two indurated, ulcerative lesions around the anus
Internal fistula opening at the right side of the dentate line
Normal mucosa in the rectum and colon
Abdominopelvic CT and MRI showed a well-defined mass
No inguinal nodal or distant metastases
Serum carcinoembryonic antigen level within normal range

differentials: Basal cell carcinoma of the anus

per_call: Basal cell carcinoma of the anus

shortlist: Squamous cell carcinoma of the anus

shortlist.label: Anal gland carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic perianal disease with recent worsening of symptoms and development of mucinous discharge

shortlist.label: Cloacogenic carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of a well-defined mass at the anorectal junction and enlarged pelvic lymph nodes

shortlist.label: Adenocarcinoma of the rectum
shortlist.why_kept: Internal fistula opening at the right side of the dentate line and normal mucosa in the rectum and colon

shortlist.label: Squamous cell carcinoma of the anus
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of indurated, ulcerative lesions around the anus

raw.rationale: Histological examination of a biopsy specimen from the indurated area revealed mucinous adenocarcinoma, which directly explains the mucinous discharge and is consistent with the patient's presentation and imaging findings.

rejected.label: Anal gland carcinoma
rejected.why: While possible, the direct histological evidence supports mucinous adenocarcinoma over this option.

rejected.label: Cloacogenic carcinoma
rejected.why: This is a type of tumor that could present similarly, but the histological findings specifically point to mucinous adenocarcinoma.

rejected.label: Adenocarcinoma of the rectum
rejected.why: The tumor's location at the anorectal junction and the presence of fistulae are more suggestive of an anal primary than a rectal primary.

rejected.label: Squamous cell carcinoma of the anus
rejected.why: The histological examination revealed mucinous adenocarcinoma, not squamous cell carcinoma, making this option incorrect.
